decisions.statement: The identifiers judged are the properties declaring a `unique`.
The identifiers judged are read from the schema.
How far a value must be alone is the unique kind its property declares.
The kind `page` is across every page and the kind `page-type` is among the pages of one type.
A page the change has is read from the change.
The index is read as this change leaves the index.
The rule is that the index files one page at a key.
A page of a page type the change itself adds is judged.
The schema is read as the change leaves the schema.
Two pages in one change with one value are refused.
No page outside the change is opened to be judged.
Working the index out does open the page type and record property pages that index names.

definition: the check refusing a page with an identifier another page already has
